name: Synthetic Short Put (Covered Call)
summary: 100 long shares plus one short call has the identical payoff to a short put at the call's strike; it is the most common structure in retail and the parity twin of a cash-secured put.

legs.strike_rule: OTM call at delta +0.25 to +0.35 (target 0.30); ATM for maximum premium at the cost of all upside

max_profit: (call_strike - entry_spot) x 100 + call_credit, capped at the strike
max_loss: (entry_spot x 100) - call_credit if the underlying goes to zero

greeks.delta: +0.65 to +0.75 per unit (100 shares less the short call delta)
greeks.theta: positive — the short call decays in your favour

when_to_use: IV rank >= 40 so the sold call is rich, on a name that is already held or is wanted at the current price. Neutral-to-mildly-bullish only: the upside is sold away above the strike.
entry_rules: LEVEL 2 legal and fully executable on Alpaca Level 3, including as a single multi-leg buy-write order (the short call is covered by the shares in the same order, which satisfies Alpaca's same-order coverage rule).

Exactly 100 shares per short call. The system must verify the share balance before submitting the call, and must never allow the share count to drop below 100 x (number of short calls) — that would create an uncovered short call, which Level 3 forbids.
Call strike selected by delta: nearest listed strike with delta in [0.25, 0.35].
Only open when IV rank >= 40 and the call credit >= 0.8% of share notional for a 30-45 DTE contract.
Skip any expiry that contains an ex-dividend date unless the call credit exceeds the dividend by 2x (see assignment_risk).
No entry with earnings inside the contract's life unless the premium is explicitly an earnings-IV trade and size is halved.
management_rules: Close the short call at 50% of the credit received, or at 21 DTE, whichever comes first.
If the call reaches 21 DTE and is OTM, roll out to the next 30-45 DTE cycle for a net credit; never roll for a debit.
If spot > call_strike and the call delta exceeds 0.80, close the call and re-evaluate: rolling up-and-out is acceptable only for a net credit.
If the share position is down more than 15% from entry, do not keep selling calls at strikes below the share cost basis — that locks in a loss on assignment.
exit_rules: MANDATORY ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the short call no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day if spot is within 1.0% of the strike or above it. Being assigned sells the shares, which for a system that must never be assigned is a failure state even though the shares cover it.

Close the short call by 15:00 ET the session BEFORE any ex-dividend date if call_extrinsic = call_mid - max(0, spot - strike) < 1.25 x declared_dividend. This is the single most common cause of surprise early assignment.
If the call is ITM at any point on expiration day, close it by 14:00 ET.
If the shares are sold for any reason, the short call must be closed in the same session — priority order: close the call first, then the shares.
assignment_risk: On the short call, and it is genuinely covered by the shares so there is no margin event. The two triggers are (1) dividend capture: an ITM call with extrinsic below the dividend will be exercised the day before the ex-date, and (2) deep ITM near expiry with extrinsic below ~$0.05. Assignment delivers the 100 shares at the strike. For a system with a never-be-assigned mandate, the dividend rule above is not optional.
buying_power: 100 shares at full cost (cash) or 50% (Reg T margin); the short call adds no requirement because it is covered. Roughly $10,000 cash or $5,000 margin on a $100 underlying.
liquidity_needs: Call OI >= 500, bid-ask <= $0.05 or 3% of mid. Share liquidity ADV >= 1,000,000.
common_mistakes: Selling calls below the share cost basis to chase premium. Letting the share count drift below 100 per call (creating a naked call). Ignoring ex-dividend dates entirely.
zero_dte_notes: 0DTE covered calls on a held position are workable but the premium is tiny and pin risk at the strike is maximal; the 15:40 ET close rule becomes the dominant consideration. Only use if the shares are genuinely wanted to be sold at the strike.
